source_text: Contra eiusmodi clamat Dominus, ab his refrenat et reuocat errantem plebem suam dicens: nolite audire sermones pseudoprophetarum, quoniam uisiones cordis eorum frustrantur eos. locuntur sed non ab ore Domini. dicunt eis qui abiciunt uerbum Dei: pax erit uobis et omnibus ambulantibus in uoluntatibus suis, omnis qui ambulat errore cordis sui non uenient super te mala. non locutus sum ad eos, et ipsi prophetauerunt. si stetissent in substantia mea et andissent uerba mea et si docuissent populum meum, conuertissem eos a malis cogitationibus eorum. hos eosdem denuo Dominus designat et denotat dicens: me dereliquerunt fontem aquae uitae et effoderunt sibi lacus detritos qui non possunt aquam portare. quando aliud baptisma praeter unum esse non possit, baptizare se opinantur: uitae fonte deserto uitalis et salutaris aquae gratiam pollicentur. non abluuntur illic homines sed potius sordidantur, nec purgantur delicta sed immo cumulantur. non Deo natiuitas illa sed diabolo filios generat. per mendacium nati ueritatis promissa non capiunt: de perfidia procreati fidei gratiam perdunt. ad pacis praemium uenire non possunt qui pacem Domini discordiae furore ruperunt.
thought_title: The Lord condemns false prophets and false baptism
orientation: Cyprian is denouncing those who set themselves up as leaders outside the Church, and now he shows that the Lord himself cries out against them and calls his wandering people back.
pass_a_gloss: Against people of this kind the Lord cries out, from these he restrains and calls back his wandering people saying: do not listen to the words of the false prophets, because the visions of their heart deceive them. They speak but not from the mouth of the Lord. They say to those who cast away the word of God: peace will be to you and to all who walk in their own desires, everyone who walks in the error of his own heart, evils will not come upon you. I have not spoken to them, and they themselves have prophesied. If they had stood in my substance and had heard my words and if they had taught my people, I would have turned them from their evil thoughts. These same ones again the Lord marks out and points out saying: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and have dug for themselves worn-out cisterns which cannot hold water. When another baptism besides the one cannot exist, they think that they baptize: with the fountain of life abandoned they promise the grace of vital and saving water. Men are not washed there but rather are made filthy, nor are sins cleansed but rather are heaped up. That birth is not for God but begets sons for the devil. Born through falsehood they do not receive the promises of truth: begotten from faithlessness they lose the grace of faith. They cannot come to the reward of peace who have broken the peace of the Lord by the fury of discord.

choices.why: Literal rendering of substantia, preserving the Old Latin wording of Jeremiah 23:22 as Cyprian quotes it; the term suggests standing in God's own reality or counsel.
Literal translation of detritos as worn-out, matching the image of broken cisterns that cannot hold water from Jeremiah 2:13.

choices.english: with the fountain of life abandoned
choices.why: Preserves the ablative absolute construction literally, showing the cause: they abandon the true source and then promise grace.
rejected: having abandoned the fountain of life
after abandoning the fountain of life

choices.why: Keeps the literal noun natiuitas, which Cyprian uses for the spiritual rebirth of baptism, contrasting true birth from God with birth from the devil.
Literal rendering of furore as fury, preserving the violent emotional force Cyprian attributes to schismatics.

pass_b_english: Against people like these the Lord cries out. He restrains his wandering people and calls them back from such men, saying: "Do not listen to the words of the false prophets, because the visions of their hearts deceive them. They speak, but not from the mouth of the Lord. They say to those who cast away the word of God: 'Peace will be yours, and to all who walk according to their own desires. Everyone who walks in the error of his own heart—no evil will come upon you.' I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied. If they had stood in my substance and heard my words, and if they had taught my people, I would have turned them from their evil thoughts" (Jeremiah 23:16-17, 21-22). The Lord points these same people out again and marks them, saying: "They have abandoned me, the fountain of living water, and dug for themselves worn-out cisterns that cannot hold water" (Jeremiah 2:13). Since there can be no baptism other than the one, they suppose they can baptize. With the fountain of life abandoned, they promise the grace of life-giving and saving water. People are not washed there but rather made filthy, nor are their sins cleansed but instead heaped up. That birth produces children not for God but for the devil. Born through a lie, they do not receive the promises of truth; begotten from faithlessness, they lose the grace of faith. They cannot come to the reward of peace, because they have broken the peace of the Lord by the fury of discord.
